title: Earth-Moon distance: 1.4 billion years ago vs today (km)

source.name: TimeOptMCMC astrochronology reconstruction of Precambrian rock layers
source.publisher: Meyers & Malinverno, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (2018)

notes: The 2018 PNAS study (Meyers, Univ. of Wisconsin; Malinverno, Columbia's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory) dated 1.4-billion-year-old rock layers and derived an Earth-Moon distance of 340,900 km and a 18.68-hour day at that time, versus today's ~384,400 km average distance.
